At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in eyelid retraction surgery, including lower eyelid retraction repair. Serving patients in Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is dedicated to providing advanced surgical solutions tailored to each patient’s unique needs.

Understanding Eyelid Retraction

Eyelid retraction occurs when the eyelid is abnormally elevated or pulled back, exposing more of the eye than normal. This condition can affect both the upper and lower eyelids, leading to symptoms such as dryness, irritation, and an altered appearance.

Causes of Eyelid Retraction

Eyelid retraction can result from various factors, including:

Thyroid Eye Disease

An autoimmune condition associated with hyperthyroidism.

Previous Surgeries

Complications or scarring from previous eyelid surgeries.

Trauma

Injury to the eyelid or surrounding structures.

Congenital Issues

Developmental abnormalities present at birth.

Neurological Conditions

Disorders affecting the muscles or nerves of the eyelid.

Symptoms of Eyelid Retraction

Common symptoms of eyelid retraction include:

Eye Dryness

Increased exposure leading to dry and irritated eyes.

Redness and Irritation

Persistent irritation due to the abnormal eyelid position.

Eye Discomfort

Discomfort and pain, especially in cases of severe retraction.

Altered Appearance

Noticeable changes in the appearance of the eyes and face.

Lower Eyelid Retraction Repair

Lower eyelid retraction repair involves surgical techniques to correct the positioning of the lower eyelid, ensuring it adequately covers the eye and functions properly. The specific approach depends on the cause and severity of the retraction.

Techniques for Lower Eyelid Retraction Repair

Tightening and Lifting

Tightening the lower eyelid and lifting it to its natural position.

Grafts and Flaps

Using tissue grafts or flaps to reconstruct and support the lower eyelid.

Canthoplasty

Reconstructing the outer corner of the eyelid to improve support and positioning.

Spacer Grafts

Inserting grafts to provide additional support and correct eyelid position.

Upper Eyelid Retraction Repair

Upper eyelid retraction repair involves repositioning the upper eyelid to a more natural and comfortable position. Techniques may include:

Releasing Scar Tissue

Addressing any scar tissue causing the retraction.

Adjusting Eyelid Muscles

Reconstructing or repositioning the muscles that lift the eyelid.

Fat or Tissue Grafts

Adding volume to support and reposition the upper eyelid.

Frequently Asked Questions | Eyelid Retraction Surgery

How Long Does Recovery Take After Eyelid Retraction Surgery?

Recovery time varies depending on the specific procedure, but most patients experience mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Full recovery typically takes a few weeks to a few months.

Will My Insurance Cover Eyelid Retraction Surgery?

Insurance coverage varies, but if the procedure is deemed medically necessary to correct functional issues, it may be covered. Our team at AestheticEye can help you navigate your insurance options.

Are There Risks Associated with Eyelid Retraction Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and complications related to anesthesia. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament.

Can Eyelid Retraction Recur After Surgery?

While eyelid retraction repair surgery is highly effective, there is a small chance of recurrence, especially if the underlying cause is not fully addressed. Regular follow-up appointments help monitor and maintain the results.

How Do I Know If I Need Eyelid Retraction Surgery?

If you experience symptoms such as chronic dryness, eye irritation, or visible misalignment of the eyelid, a consultation with our surgeons can determine if eyelid retraction surgery is right for you.
